skill.name: postgresql-table-design
skill.description: Design PostgreSQL schemas with practical guidance for data types, constraints, indexes, partitioning, and schema evolution.
skill.summary: Plan PostgreSQL tables, indexes, constraints, and data types using production-focused design rules.
skill.author: wshobson

content.value_statement: PostgreSQL schemas can fail when data types, constraints, and indexes are chosen without workload context. This skill guides table design with PostgreSQL-specific rules for durable, performant, and maintainable schemas.
actual_capabilities: Recommends PostgreSQL data types for identifiers, money, time, strings, JSONB, arrays, ranges, and network values.
Guides primary keys, foreign keys, unique constraints, checks, exclusion constraints, and row-level security policies.
Explains index choices, including B-tree, GIN, GiST, BRIN, composite, partial, expression, and covering indexes.
Covers partitioning patterns for large tables, time-series data, insert-heavy workloads, and maintenance windows.
Highlights safe schema evolution issues such as transactional DDL, concurrent indexes, volatile defaults, and dependency order.
Provides examples for users, orders, and JSONB profile tables using PostgreSQL-focused conventions.
limitations: Does not connect to a live database or inspect production query plans.
Does not benchmark workload performance or prove an index is useful.
Focuses on PostgreSQL and may not apply to MySQL, SQL Server, or SQLite.
Does not replace security, privacy, or compliance review for regulated data models.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Product Schema
use_cases.description: Create table structures with suitable keys, constraints, timestamps, and indexes before implementation begins.

use_cases.title: Review Database Design Choices
use_cases.description: Check an existing design for weak data types, missing foreign key indexes, JSONB misuse, or unsafe defaults.

use_cases.title: Model High-Volume Tables
use_cases.description: Choose partitioning, BRIN indexes, reduced indexes, and staging patterns for large or insert-heavy PostgreSQL workloads.

prompt_templates.title: Design Basic Tables
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new schema.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design PostgreSQL tables for this feature: [describe feature]. Include keys, required columns, data types, constraints, and basic indexes.

prompt_templates.title: Review Existing Schema
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of a proposed design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this PostgreSQL schema for data type choices, constraints, foreign key indexes, and naming issues: [paste schema].

prompt_templates.title: Optimize for Workload
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced design based on query patterns.
prompt_templates.prompt: Given these PostgreSQL tables and query patterns, recommend indexes, partitioning, and schema changes. Explain each tradeoff clearly.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Migration Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced schema evolution for production systems.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PostgreSQL schema evolution plan for these changes: [describe changes]. Include lock risks, concurrent index needs, and rollback considerations.

output_examples.input: A user and order feature needs durable PostgreSQL tables with searchable email and order history.
output: A schema outline with separate user and order tables, identity keys, required timestamps, and checked order status values.
Index recommendations for email lookup, order ownership, and created date filtering.
Notes explaining why numeric money fields and timestamptz event fields are preferred.

output_examples.input: A product profile table stores optional settings and searchable attributes in JSONB.
output: Guidance to keep core relational fields in columns and reserve JSONB for optional attributes.
Recommendations for GIN indexing, generated columns for scalar searches, and constraints for valid JSONB shape.

output_examples.input: A telemetry table will receive millions of rows per day and most queries filter by time.
output: A time-based partitioning plan with minimal indexes for insert performance.
Advice to consider BRIN indexes, bulk loading patterns, and rebuildable staging tables.

best_practices: Start with normalized tables, then denormalize only after measured query pressure justifies the added maintenance cost.
Add indexes for proven access paths, including foreign key columns, frequent filters, sort keys, and joins.
Use PostgreSQL-specific types and constraints to enforce meaning close to the data.
anti_patterns: Using JSONB for core relational data that needs constraints, joins, and stable query patterns.
Adding broad indexes before query patterns are known, especially on insert-heavy tables.
Choosing legacy or weak types such as serial, timestamp without time zone, money, or fixed char columns.
